108: Discussion. Zinc is required for immune function, growth and wound healing, and after iron is the mineral most frequently deficient in rice-based diets, so that a higher content is preferable. Zinc loading is contingent upon the HMA2 and HMA4 transporters and upon remobilisation during grain filling, the element being retained in the aleurone largely as phytate salts.

(2026) that polishing is of greater consequence than the thermal step. 123: Discussion. Lightness measures the degree to which the product has remained pale. It declines with browning and with the inward migration of pigments, so that a higher value generally denotes gentler processing. Lightness declines as browning products accumulate and as pericarp pigments dissolve and migrate inward, and cultivars richer in reducing sugar and free amino nitrogen brown further under an identical treatment.
124: Comparable observations appear in the literature. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that darkening proceeds from pigment migration and browning; Srisang et al. (2021) that lightness declines as the thermal treatment becomes more severe; Panda et al. (2021) that shorter heating yields a lighter product at equivalent moisture loss; and Akter et al. (2025) that a darker product was nonetheless preferred overall. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Dudeshwar, Kalojira, Lal Badshabhog and Radhatilak ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.

130: Discussion. The a* value is signed: a positive value places the sample on the red side of the green-to-red axis and a negative value on the green side. Redness increases as browning proceeds, so that a lower value is preferred. Redness rises as melanoidins and their coloured precursors accumulate, the rate being contingent upon the reducing sugars and free amino acids the cultivar supplies.

137: Discussion. Yellowness arises from the migration of bran pigments into the endosperm and from early browning products. Except where a golden colour is required, a lower value is preferable. It derives from carotenoids and flavonoids conveyed inward from the pericarp during hydration together with early browning products, so that cultivars richer in pigment return higher values.

(2021) that yellowing is proportional to the heat load; Devi and Badwaik (2022) that colour readings track pigment composition; and Oliveira et al. (2026) that final colour is contingent upon pigment and processing jointly. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Dudeshwar, Kataribhog, Lal Badshabhog and Radhunipagal ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

This parameter measures the overall colour distance between the product and the raw grain; a smaller value denotes that the grain has altered in texture without appreciable alteration in appearance. It integrates all three colour coordinates and therefore registers both pigment migration and browning, each of which scales with the substrate the cultivar provides.

152: Discussion. Spreading in dilute alkali is inversely related to gelatinisation temperature: a higher spreading value denotes that the grain gelatinises at a lower temperature and therefore cooks in less time and with less fuel. Disintegration in alkali is contingent upon the crystalline order of the starch granule, which is governed by amylopectin chain length under starch synthase IIa, so that the ranking follows gelatinisation temperature.
153: Published work is concordant. Little et al. (1958) established the alkali test as the routine measure of gelatinisation; Bocevska et al. (2009) determined that the spreading score corresponds to instrumental gelatinisation; Ayamdoo et al. (2014) that cultivars of differing gelatinisation temperature respond differently; and Armstrong et al. (2022) that the spreading value may be predicted by near infrared spectroscopy. Kalonunia returned the most favourable value here and is therefore the cultivar to select where a high value is required.
